title: Priapism: Emergency Assessment and Urology Management

evidenceAudit.scope: Adult men with an erection lasting more than 4 hours in the emergency department (ED): separating ischaemic from non-ischaemic priapism, corporal blood gas, aspiration with intracavernosal phenylephrine, escalation to urology for shunt surgery, sickle cell disease, counselling about erectile dysfunction, and recurrent (stuttering) priapism. Uses the American Urological Association (AUA) and Sexual Medicine Society of North America (SMSNA) 2022 guideline, a drug-information summary of its phenylephrine dosing and the phenylephrine product information. Children are excluded.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-22.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi priapism guideline was found.
The AUA/SMSNA guideline page opened did not give phenylephrine doses; the dose comes from a university drug-information summary of the guideline.
Intracavernosal use is outside the phenylephrine product licence, which covers intravenous use only.
Numerical corporal blood gas cut-offs were not given on the page opened; ischaemic blood is described as hypoxic, hypercarbic and acidotic.
Local anaesthetic penile block technique and doses were not sourced.
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.

pathophysiology.summary: Priapism is a persistent erection lasting hours beyond, or unrelated to, sexual stimulation; the guideline uses more than 4 hours (AUA/SMSNA priapism 2022, Section Executive summary). Ischaemic priapism traps hypoxic, hypercarbic, acidotic blood in the corpora and is an emergency (AUA/SMSNA priapism 2022, Section Definitions). Non-ischaemic priapism is not an emergency and can be observed first (AUA/SMSNA priapism 2022, Statement 23). The chance of recovering erectile function falls with time and is low beyond 36 hours (AUA/SMSNA priapism 2022, Statement 7).

symptoms: Erection lasting more than 4 hours (AUA/SMSNA priapism 2022, Section Executive summary).
Pain is typical of ischaemic priapism (AUA/SMSNA priapism 2022, Statement 1).
physicalSigns: Rigid corpora cavernosa with soft glans in ischaemic priapism (AUA/SMSNA priapism 2022, Statement 1).
Perineal or genital trauma in non-ischaemic priapism (AUA/SMSNA priapism 2022, Statement 1).
redFlags: Ischaemic priapism: urgent aspiration and phenylephrine (AUA/SMSNA priapism 2022, Statement 8).
Failure of aspiration and phenylephrine: urology for distal shunt (AUA/SMSNA priapism 2022, Statement 10).
More than 36 hours: erectile recovery unlikely; discuss prosthesis (AUA/SMSNA priapism 2022, Statements 7 and 14).
Sickle cell disease: do not delay intracavernosal treatment for systemic measures (AUA/SMSNA priapism 2022, Statement 18).
precipitants: Intracavernosal erectile drugs and other medicines (AUA/SMSNA priapism 2022, Statement 1).
Perineal or penile trauma in non-ischaemic priapism (AUA/SMSNA priapism 2022, Statement 1).

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Painless, partly rigid, often after trauma; corporal blood not hypoxic; observe first (AUA/SMSNA priapism 2022, Statements 2 and 23).
Recurrent ischaemic episodes; prevention strategies uncertain (AUA/SMSNA priapism 2022, Statement 16).

ruleIn.modalityTarget: Corporal oxygen, carbon dioxide and pH
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Obtain at first presentation to separate ischaemic from non-ischaemic (AUA/SMSNA priapism 2022, Statement 2).
ruleIn.normalValue: Values similar to arterial blood: pH about 7.40, oxygen near arterial levels (typical values)

clinicalManagement.title: Assess and classify
actions: Take history of duration, pain, drugs and trauma, and examine genitals and perineum (AUA/SMSNA priapism 2022, Statement 1).
Send corporal blood gas (AUA/SMSNA priapism 2022, Statement 2).

clinicalManagement.title: Treat ischaemic priapism
actions: Corporal aspiration with or without irrigation and intracavernosal phenylephrine (see Medicines) (AUA/SMSNA priapism 2022, Statement 8).
Monitor blood pressure and heart rate during injections (AUA/SMSNA priapism 2022, Statement 9).
Counsel that erectile dysfunction may follow (AUA/SMSNA priapism 2022, Statement 6).

clinicalManagement.title: Escalate failures
clinicalManagement.timeframe: If no detumescence after about 1 hour of treatment
actions: Refer to urology for distal corporoglanular shunt, with or without tunnelling (AUA/SMSNA priapism 2022, Statements 10 and 11).
After 36 hours or failed shunts, discuss penile prosthesis (AUA/SMSNA priapism 2022, Statements 14 and 15).

clinicalManagement.title: Sickle cell disease
actions: Give standard intracavernosal treatment without waiting for hydration, oxygen or transfusion (AUA/SMSNA priapism 2022, Statement 18).

clinicalManagement.title: Non-ischaemic priapism
actions: Explain it is not an emergency and offer observation with urology follow-up (AUA/SMSNA priapism 2022, Statement 23).

regimens.indication: Detumescence in acute ischaemic priapism after aspiration
regimens.dose: 100 to 500 micrograms in 1 mL 0.9% sodium chloride per injection, repeated as needed; stop if blood pressure changes or if the erection persists after repeated injections and aspiration for an hour or more (UIC 2022 summary of AUA/SMSNA). Prepare from the 10 mg/mL concentrate by dilution (Phenylephrine SmPC, Section 6.6).
regimens.frequency: Repeat injections at short intervals as needed
regimens.duration: Until detumescence or about 1 hour, then escalate to urology
adjustments: Use caution in cardiovascular disease, bradycardia, arteriosclerosis and older age (Phenylephrine SmPC, Section 4.4; UIC 2022 summary).
No renal or hepatic adjustment stated.

monitoring: Blood pressure and heart rate with each injection (AUA/SMSNA priapism 2022, Statement 9).
Chest pain or palpitations: possible coronary vasospasm (UIC 2022 summary).
contraindications: Severe hypertension or peripheral vascular disease (Phenylephrine SmPC, Section 4.3).
Non-selective monoamine oxidase inhibitors now or within 2 weeks (Phenylephrine SmPC, Section 4.3).

medicationPlan.note: Phenylephrine is given intracavernosally after aspiration, outside its intravenous licence, ideally pre-mixed by pharmacy (UIC 2022 summary of AUA/SMSNA). SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Erection lasting more than 4 hours beyond or unrelated to sexual stimulation (AUA/SMSNA priapism 2022, Section Executive summary).
Corporal blood gas hypoxic, hypercarbic and acidotic (AUA/SMSNA priapism 2022, Statement 2 and Section Definitions).
Penile duplex Doppler ultrasound may help (AUA/SMSNA priapism 2022, Statement 3).

teaching.scope: Adult men with an erection lasting more than 4 hours in the emergency department (ED): separating ischaemic from non-ischaemic priapism, corporal blood gas, aspiration with intracavernosal phenylephrine, escalation to urology for shunt surgery, sickle cell disease, counselling about erectile dysfunction, and recurrent (stuttering) priapism. Uses the American Urological Association (AUA) and Sexual Medicine Society of North America (SMSNA) 2022 guideline, a drug-information summary of its phenylephrine dosing and the phenylephrine product information. Children are excluded.
learningObjectives: Separate ischaemic from non-ischaemic priapism with a blood gas.
Aspirate and inject phenylephrine for ischaemic priapism.
Monitor blood pressure and heart rate.
Escalate to urology when treatment fails.
pitfalls: Waiting for exchange transfusion in sickle cell disease.
Giving phenylephrine without blood pressure monitoring.
Treating non-ischaemic priapism as an emergency.
keyPoints: Sickle cell disease does not delay local treatment.

patientEducation: An erection lasting more than 4 hours is an emergency; come to hospital straight away.
Long episodes can cause permanent erection problems.
Tell your doctor about all medicines, especially injections for erections.
lifestyleAndDiet: Avoid recreational drugs and do not exceed prescribed erectile medicine doses.
mdtReferrals: Emergency physician; urologist; haematologist for sickle cell disease; pharmacy for phenylephrine preparation.
dischargeCriteria: Detumescence achieved, observed without recurrence, counselled about erectile dysfunction and recurrence, urology follow-up arranged.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Urology follow-up for erectile function and recurrent episodes; haematology review in sickle cell disease (AUA/SMSNA priapism 2022, Statements 6, 16 and 18).
